summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn opened by sharing about a recent trip to Los Angeles, where he and a team went simply to show love to firefighters and their families. They prayed with them, listened to them, gave out his book, and sang worship songs in a firehouse. Standing among the burned neighborhoods of Altadena, he saw a picture of what many people face spiritually, emotionally, relationally, and physically: fires in marriages, families, health, and hearts. He found encouragement in Isaiah 43:2, where God promises to be with us in the waters and the fire, and in Isaiah 61:3, where God gives beauty for ashes.

From there Pastor Travis preached a message titled "Get in the Game." His central call was for believers to move from being spectators and consumers to being participators and servants. He explained that every Christian is called to be a minister, since the word means to serve, and he pointed to Jesus, who came not to be served but to serve. He gave two directives. First, develop a burden for the broken by asking God for eyes to see the need and a heart to act. He used the Good Samaritan in Luke 10 and Jesus' mission statement in Luke 4 to show that seeing without doing is not enough. Second, be a blessing to the broken. Citing Galatians 6:2, he reminded the church that we are blessed in order to bless others, and that the most powerful word we can say to God is yes.

He described what saying yes has looked like: Books for the Broken, which gives away his book of hope and healing to firehouses, hospitals, rehab centers, a refuge in Thailand, and pastors in Mexico. He also read a message from Thailand reporting that a woman who had been paralyzed stood and walked after receiving a book.

Pastor Travis celebrated people being saved and baptized, called the church to serve through the volunteer Dream Team, and introduced a revamped membership class on February 16 as a way to move from the crowd to the core. He reminded the church that we are one body (1 Corinthians 12:27), that each person's gifts are meant for others (1 Peter 4:10), and that we should look to the interests of others (Philippians 2:4). He closed by leading the congregation in a prayer of surrender, "my answer is yes," and invited anyone who wanted to receive Jesus to pray for salvation.
mainPoints: God calls us to move from spectators to participators, serving as ministers in the way Jesus came to serve.
Develop a burden for the broken by asking God for eyes to see the need and a heart that acts, not just sees.
We are blessed to be a blessing, and the most powerful response to God is a simple yes, lived out through generosity, serving, and belonging to the body of Christ.

and provide for those who grieve in Zion: to bestow on them a crown of beauty instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, and a garment of praise instead of a spirit of despair. They will be called oaks of righteousness, a planting of the Lord for the display of his splendor.

But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came where the man was; and when he saw him, he took pity on him. He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put the man on his own donkey, brought him to an inn and took care of him. The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. "Look after him," he said, "and when I return, I will reimburse you for any extra expense you may have."

The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor.
Carry each other's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!
Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms.
Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
If you declare with your mouth, "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

Monday.scripture: Isaiah 43:2: "When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and when you walk through the fire, you will not be burned."
Monday.focus: God is with us in every fire and flood of life.
Monday.action: Reach out by call or text to someone you know who is in a hard season. Ask, "How can I help you this week?" and listen well.
Monday.prayer: Lord, thank you that you walk with me through the waters and the fire. Help me to bring your comfort to someone who feels alone today. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Luke 10:33: "But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came where the man was; and when he saw him, he took pity on him."
Tuesday.focus: Ask God for eyes to see the needs around you.
Tuesday.action: Spend ten minutes today noticing the people around you at work, home, or in your neighborhood. Write down one need you see and one way you could meet it.
Tuesday.prayer: God, give me eyes to see and a heart to do something. Open my awareness to the people you place in my path. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Galatians 6:2: "Carry each other's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ."
Wednesday.focus: Bear one another's burdens in practical ways.
Wednesday.action: Do one practical act of help today, such as bringing a meal, running an errand, or offering a ride to someone who is struggling.
Wednesday.prayer: Father, give me a burden for the broken. Show me how to carry someone else's load with love and patience. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: 1 Peter 4:10: "Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms."
Thursday.focus: Your gifts are meant to be a gift to others.
Thursday.action: Write down three strengths or gifts God has given you. Then take one step toward serving with them, such as signing up to volunteer with a ministry team at church.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, thank you for the gifts you have given me. Teach me to use them for others and not only for myself. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Matthew 20:28: "just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
Friday.focus: Follow the humble, servant heart of Jesus.
Friday.action: Do a quiet act of kindness for someone without seeking credit, such as paying for a stranger's coffee or meal or giving a generous gift to a worthy cause.
Friday.prayer: Jesus, thank you for serving me and giving your life for me. Make my heart humble and ready to serve others. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: 1 Corinthians 12:27: "Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it."
Saturday.focus: Move from the crowd to the core by belonging and saying yes to God.
Saturday.action: Pray about your next step in the church family, such as signing up for the membership class, baptism, or a serving team. Then take that step or tell a friend about your decision.
Saturday.prayer: God, my answer is yes. Help me to be a participator and not a spectator, and to play my part in your body for your glory. Amen.

title: Get In The Game
speaker: Pastor Travis Hearn
